records.name: Platform Migration
records.definition: The ability to move a system to a different platform with little or no rework.

records.name: Platform Optimization
records.definition: The degree to which staying portable across platforms forgoes optimizations specific to any one of them.

records.name: Platform-Specific Coupling
records.definition: Binding code to one platform's APIs and assumptions, so it cannot run elsewhere without rewriting.

records.name: Cross-Platform Deployment
records.definition: The ability to deploy the same software unchanged across different operating systems and platforms.

records.name: Native Optimization
records.definition: The degree to which staying platform-independent forgoes optimizations native to a specific platform.

records.name: OS/Vendor Lock-In
records.definition: Depending on one operating system or vendor's proprietary features, so switching away becomes costly or impossible.

records.name: Platform Abstraction
records.definition: The requirement that platform-specific details sit behind an abstraction the rest of the system depends on.

records.name: Reliable Deployment
records.definition: The ability to deploy with confidence because every environment behaves the same way.

records.name: Snowflake Environments
records.definition: Environments each configured by hand into unique, unreproducible states, so what works in one fails in another.

records.name: Externalized Config
records.definition: The requirement that configuration live outside the container image so one image runs in any environment.

records.name: Host-Coupled Deployment
records.definition: Deploying software that depends on specifics of its host machine, so it cannot be moved or reproduced elsewhere.

records.name: Image Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which packaging everything into a container image grows the image and its maintenance burden.

records.name: Image Definition
records.definition: A declarative file specifying how a container image is built from a base and its dependencies.

records.name: Repeatable Runtime Packaging
records.definition: The ability to package an application and its runtime into one reproducible, portable unit.

records.name: Automated Provisioning
records.definition: The ability to create and configure infrastructure automatically from declarative definitions.

records.name: Manual Infrastructure Changes
records.definition: Changing infrastructure by hand instead of through code, so its state is undocumented and unreproducible.

records.name: Version Control
records.definition: A system that records changes to files over time so any version can be recovered, compared, or audited.

records.name: Applicable Standard
records.definition: The requirement that the relevant external standard a system must meet be identified and adhered to.

records.name: Certification/Compatibility
records.definition: The ability to certify a system and interoperate with others by conforming to a shared standard.

records.name: Innovation/Flexibility
records.definition: The degree to which conforming to an external standard limits the freedom to innovate beyond it.

records.name: Proprietary Deviation
records.definition: Deviating from a shared standard with proprietary extensions, breaking interoperability with conformant systems.

records.name: Adapter/Port Abstraction
records.definition: A boundary abstraction separating core logic from external protocols via port interfaces and pluggable adapters.

records.name: Protocol Swap
records.definition: The ability to switch the transport or wire protocol without changing core domain logic.

records.name: Protocol-Coupled Domain Logic
records.definition: Domain logic written directly against a specific protocol, so changing the protocol means rewriting the core.

records.name: Protocol-Specific Features
records.definition: The degree to which staying protocol-independent forgoes features unique to any one protocol.

records.name: Config Schema
records.definition: A schema defining the structure, types, and defaults of a system's externalized configuration.

records.name: Config Sprawl
records.definition: The degree to which externalizing configuration across many sources scatters it and makes it hard to track.

records.name: Environment-Specific Deployment
records.definition: The ability to deploy one build into different environments by supplying environment-specific configuration.

records.name: Secure Config Handling
records.definition: The requirement that secrets and sensitive configuration be stored and injected securely, never hardcoded.

records.name: Deploy Time
records.definition: The degree to which replacing whole instances rather than patching them in place lengthens deployment time.

records.name: Deterministic Redeploys

distinctFrom.reason: Deterministic redeploys are the identical result from one fixed definition, while replacement over mutation is the method of discarding instances instead of changing them.

records.definition: The ability to redeploy infrastructure identically every time from one fixed definition.

records.name: In-Place Server Mutation
records.definition: Modifying running servers in place over time, so their state drifts and can no longer be reproduced.

records.name: Instance Replacement over Mutation
records.definition: The ability to update infrastructure by replacing instances wholesale rather than mutating them in place.
